correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the proof for smooth n-dimensional intersections of n+1 split quadrics in P^(2n+1) over C with the assumed free fixed-point-free sign involution; n is EVEN and at least 4. Integral complete-intersection Lefschetz below degree n yields H0Y=Z, H1Y=0, H2Y=Z (hyperplane), H3Y=0 and pi1Y=0. The involution acts trivially on H2Y; integral Cartan–Leray for C2 has E2^{p,q}=H^p(C2,H^qY). Every total-degree-three term is zero, so H3(T,Z)=0 without hidden differential, and surviving terms in degree two give 0→Z/2→H2T→Z→0, split. H1,H2 of O_T vanish by finite étale averaging and Hodge/Lefschetz; exponential sequence identifies Pic(T)=H2(T,Z) and H2(T,O*_T)=0, hence analytic/cohomological and algebraic Azumaya Brauer vanish. Residue top-form changes by determinant (-1)^(n+1)=-1 for even n, giving nontrivial order-two canonical class. This excludes n=2 and nonfree members. The source parity script is confirmatory only, not the proof.

value.rationale: Computing the Brauer group of a natural family of smooth Enriques-type Calabi–Yau quotients in every higher even dimension is an independently useful exact invariant: despite persistent nontrivial canonical order-two torsion, Brauer becomes zero, unlike Enriques surfaces. It resolves a concrete previously unevaluated invariant for an identified geometric family through a uniform proof; it is more than a bare restatement of the Cartan–Leray formalism.

limitations: An unindexed all-free-C2 Calabi–Yau quotient proposition may subsume this straightforward low-degree spectral-sequence application.
Varieties must be smooth and fixed-point-free; the n=2 Enriques surface is deliberately excluded.
